newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ shares a long-term buy - ING.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ shares a long-term buy - ING.

text.p: Shares of VSZ a.s., Slovakia's largest steel producer, are a long-term buy despite an expected decrease in second half profits, an investor report issued by ING Barings said on Tuesday.

The report said that while second half results are forecast to be weaker following surprisingly strong first half results, the VSZ share price was likely to benefit from sector rotation into cyclical stocks over the next six months.

"Taking country and company risks into account, we rate the stock a long-term buy," ING Barings said in its September report, putting its recommendation at 645 crowns, as of August 30. On Monday VSZ shares closed at 630 crowns on the Bratislava Stock Exchange.
"VSZ shares currently suffers from a Slovak capital market anomaly," Dusan Sykora, a broker at ING Barings told Reuters. "It (trading with VSZ) can wake up as surprisingly as it fell into silence."
High capacity utilisation and price resilience have been a key to good result of VSZ in the first half of this year, the report said.
"VSZ's results, according to Slovak accounting standards, show a strong progression in net profit towards our full year forecast of 1.25 billion crowns," the report said.
ING Barings said it was sticking to its forecast of a full year fall in net profit, under international accounting standards, to 1.25 billion crowns from 2.548 billion.

"We remain nervous of increasing our forecast because of the lack of transparency in the interim figures and the potential for one-off costs and increased financial costs in the second half as a result of VSZ's recent acquisitions in the Slovak banking and insurance industry," it said.
Last August, VSZ announced the acquisition of a 14.6 percent stake in the third largest Slovak bank, IRB and a 20 percent stake in Slovenska Poistovna, the leading Slovak insurer.
